title: CLAUDE.md prescribes a check-wait predicate that can never pass here: skipped non-required jobs are not "success"
description:
The repository profile in CLAUDE.md records a newest-per-context wait predicate -- select(.conclusion!="success") over the latest run of every context, asserting the count is zero -- and calls it "the shape to copy". It cannot be satisfied in this repository.

Measured 2026-09-16 on PR #157 head 3bb65aa: six contexts reported. source-gates, Tracker integrity and lore check succeeded; candidate-bundle, matrix.target and native-execution-receipt concluded "skipped", because they are gated off pull_request. None of those three is in the required set on main, mergeStateStatus was CLEAN, and the PR merged cleanly -- but the predicate returned 3. A background poll built on it literally as written hung and had to be killed. The poll that worked filtered to the three required context names first.

The profile already records the skipped-jobs fact in its own bullet ("candidate-bundle, matrix.target and native-execution-receipt all reported SKIPPED while mergeStateStatus was CLEAN"), so the file contradicts itself two sections apart.

The fleet reference is not wrong and this is not a fleet-wide change. opum-workflow 0.8.2 skills/opum-sdlc/references/promotion.md pulls the required contexts by name from the ruleset and asserts each is present and passed; its group_by snippet is a read of the latest conclusion per context, explicitly not the wait predicate. This repository's copy diverged from it. Confirmed by reading that file, and independently by opum-agent 2026-09-17.

Do not resolve this by switching to mergeStateStatus. On a dev-to-main promotion PR the manual-fast-forward tripwire is red by design, so that field reads BLOCKED or UNSTABLE while every required context is green. Only the required-set intersection is correct on both PR shapes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The CLAUDE.md profile no longer prescribes a bare select(.conclusion!="success") predicate; it intersects with the required set by name, read from the ruleset rather than hardcoded
The correction cites opum-workflow skills/opum-sdlc/references/promotion.md as the canonical form, so the two stop contradicting each other
The profile states why mergeStateStatus is not the alternative: the promotion-PR tripwire makes it read BLOCKED/UNSTABLE on an all-green required set
The two standing observations about promotion PRs never reaching CLEAN and the post-push mergeStateStatus race are folded into the same paragraph rather than left as separate session knowledge

plan: 1. Verify the fleet reference (opum-workflow 0.8.2 skills/opum-sdlc/references/promotion.md) rather than accepting the orchestrator report of it
2. Replace the bare no-failures predicate in CLAUDE.md with the required-set intersection read from the ruleset, marked as a correction and citing how it got in
3. Correct the mergeStateStatus prescription: false on promotion PRs (promotion-is-manual fails by design), and vacuously CLEAN right after a push
4. Prove the documented snippet both rejects and accepts against a real head SHA
finalSummary:
CLAUDE.md prescribed a check-wait predicate that could never pass in this repository, and the same section told readers to fall back on mergeStateStatus, which is wrong on exactly the PR shape where being wrong stalls a delivery forever. Both are now corrected, in one paragraph, with the correction marked rather than silently repaired.

The defect: [... |select(.conclusion!="success")] | length == 0 over the newest run of every context asserts that no context is anything other than success. That is only safe where every reporting context is required. Measured on PR #157 head 3bb65aa -- source-gates, Tracker integrity and lore check succeeded while candidate-bundle, matrix.target and native-execution-receipt concluded "skipped" (gated off pull_request), so the predicate returned 3 on a PR whose mergeStateStatus was CLEAN and which merged cleanly. A background poll built on it hung and had to be killed. The profile already recorded the skipped-jobs fact two sections away, so the file contradicted itself.

How it got in, recorded in the file because that is what lets the next reader find their own copy: the predicate was lifted out of a cross-session message and never run against this repository's own check set. The fleet reference was never wrong -- opum-workflow 0.8.2 skills/opum-sdlc/references/promotion.md reads the required contexts by name from the ruleset and asserts each is present and passed, and its group_by snippet is explicitly a READ of the latest conclusion per context, not the wait predicate. This copy collapsed the two. Verified by reading that file directly rather than accepting opum-agent's report of it; their reading was correct in every clause.

What replaces it: the required-set intersection, names pulled from repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/rules/branches/main so the guard tracks the rule rather than a copy that can drift from it, asserting each context is PRESENT as well as passed, behind a non-empty guard because `all` over an empty array is vacuously true and [] is exactly what the API returns in the seconds before runs register.

The second half: the "so do not count rows at all -- read mergeStateStatus" prescription is withdrawn. It holds on a task PR into dev. It is false on a dev-to-main promotion PR, because .github/workflows/promotion-guardrails.yml runs promotion-is-manual, which exits 1 BY DESIGN to stop anyone using the merge button, beside main-is-fast-forward-of-dev which reports skipped because it is scoped to the push. Neither is in the ruleset, deliberately, and that file's header explains why adding them would make the correct promotion path permanently unpushable. Measured on promotion PR #158 (2026-09-17): promotion-is-manual failure, main-is-fast-forward-of-dev skipped, all three required contexts green. A promotion PR here never reaches CLEAN. Confirmed fleet-wide, n=3. The same field also reads CLEAN right after a push because no checks exist yet rather than because any passed -- one field, two failures, opposite signs, and nothing in the value says which you have.

Verification, both halves against a real head rather than argued: the documented snippet was run against promotion head bdf4b61 while source-gates was still in flight and correctly reported ["in_progress","success","success"] with a non-zero exit; the same command on the same head returned exit 0 once source-gates finished. It also correctly distinguishes ABSENT from a passing conclusion. lore check exits 0 locally (63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings) and in CI.

Delivered as PR #159 into dev, head 1c3b680. CI on that exact head: Tracker integrity run 35164842323 success, lore check run 35164842234 success, Prepublication qualification run 35164842226 success. No source files change; this is profile prose and one tracker record.
